state_program_name: Community Residence for Individuals with Developmental Disabilities (group home, supervised apartment, supportive living) licensed by the NJ DHS Office of Licensing under N.J.A.C. 10:44A; services approved and paid through DDD as Individual Supports under the Community Care Program / Supports Program (NJ FamilyCare Comprehensive Demonstration, Section 1115), fee-for-service

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its community residences for individuals with developmental disabilities in New Jersey. These are provider-managed group homes, supervised apartments and supportive living arrangements licensed by the NJ Department of Human Services (DHS) Office of Licensing under **N.J.A.C. 10:44A**. Services are approved and paid through the Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDD) as Individual Supports under the Community Care Program / Supports Program (NJ FamilyCare Comprehensive Demonstration, Section 1115), fee-for-service.

The manual does the following:

- It meets the written procedure manual requirement of **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2**. Under that rule the licensee develops and implements the manual and reviews its procedures annually. Each procedure is designed around normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning, and has a unique title, a purpose, sequential steps, staff responsibilities, and reporting and recording requirements.
- It gives staff one consistent, written standard for protecting the rights, health, safety and dignity of the people **[AGENCY NAME]** supports, and for the quality of their services.
- It gives the Office of Licensing a document it can review. Under **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(i)**, a new applicant submits the procedure manual to the Office of Licensing before opening a residence, and the Office approves it if it meets 10:44A-2.2.
- It makes the licensee's purposes and a description of its services available to individuals, parents, guardians, advocates and the general public, as **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.1(a)** requires.

**Scope.** This manual covers provider-managed group homes and supervised apartments licensed under N.J.A.C. 10:44A (**N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.1**). It does not cover owner-occupied Family Care / Skill Development living arrangements, which are licensed under **N.J.A.C. 10:44B**, or head-injury residences, which fall under **N.J.A.C. 10:44C**.

**Terminology.** Terms such as *community residence*, *supervised apartment*, *direct support professional*, *governing authority*, *executive director*, *Central Registry*, *critical information* and *behavior support plan* are used as defined in **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3**.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

**1. Customize it before use.** This is a template. Every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder, and every other bracketed item (names, titles, addresses, phone numbers, schedules of charges and fees, program description, table of organization), must be replaced with **[AGENCY NAME]**'s actual information. Procedures must also be fitted to the agency's real program, residences and staffing. Do not submit or implement the manual with placeholders left in it.

**2. Have it adopted by the governing body.** The manual takes effect when **[AGENCY NAME]**'s governing authority formally adopts it. Record the adoption date, the approving body and the signature of the authorized officer on the adoption page: **[ADOPTION DATE / SIGNATURE]**.

**3. Submit it for review.** A new applicant first completes the DDD Combined Application and Attestation for Individual Supports Provider. After the application is approved and before a residence opens, the applicant submits this manual to the Office of Licensing. After the manual is approved, job descriptions for every position on the table of organization go to DDD for review (**N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(i)**). Check the Office of Licensing about whether a licensee that already operates residences with an approved manual must resubmit.

**4. Find a policy quickly.**
- The manual follows the numbered order of required contents in **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b)1-22**, so a reviewer can match each procedure to its citation.
- **Appendix A** is the crosswalk. It maps every item in the official review list to the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use it to prepare for inspections and to confirm nothing required is missing.
- Each procedure has a title, purpose, sequential steps, staff responsibilities and reporting/recording requirements (**N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a)**).

**5. Keep it current.**
- Review every procedure at least annually, as 10:44A-2.2(a) requires. Document the review date and any changes.
- Revise it promptly when rules, DDD policies, rates or Office of Licensing guidance change. The chapter was readopted effective February 17, 2026, and DHS has said further rulemaking may be necessary. The section text this manual was built on is the 2023-amended text, so recheck it against the current rule each year.
- Keep a version log of revisions, approvals and the date each change was communicated to staff.

**6. Train staff on it.**
- Every employee must be trained on the policies relevant to their duties. Under **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.7(c)**, this covers all relevant policies not covered in orientation, delivered by a qualified trainer.
- Orientation must cover the New Employee Orientation Checklist (**N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b)4**, which incorporates 10:44A-2.6(a)1-8).
- Keep training records in the administrative office, with a curriculum or training plan and dated trainer and trainee signatures (**N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.7(e)**).
- When a procedure changes, retrain affected staff and document it.

**7. Verify flagged items.** Some rule sections summarized in the framework below were only partly confirmed, namely the personnel TB screening interval (2.4), personal funds subsection (2.10), record contents and retention (2.9), and the Health and Safety (Subchapter 5) and Fire Safety (Subchapter 6) provisions. Confirm the current text of each against the official N.J.A.C. before finalizing the related policies.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

### Governing rules

The rules below are cited by their exact cite text. Where only part of a section was confirmed, that is noted. Confirm current text before relying on a provision.

**Licensing standards: N.J.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 44A**
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.1** (Purpose and scope): minimum requirements for residential services to people with developmental disabilities in provider-managed group homes and supervised apartments. Licensing is voluntary where no resident needs personal guidance, as decided by the planning team.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3** (Definitions): defines the terms used in this manual.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4** (Application for licensure): the Combined Application and Attestation, criminal history clearance for agency heads under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-63 through 69, application timelines, the Office of Licensing's review of the procedure manual before opening, DHS inspection without limitation or notice, annual on-site inspection, and grounds that bar licensure.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.1** (General requirements): the licensee's purposes and services description must be available to the public. Other subsections were not read.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2** (Development and maintenance of procedure manual): the 22 required manual contents.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.4** (Personnel): employee screening, including a TB screen. Confirm the current subsection and any repeat-testing interval.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.5** (Minimum staff qualifications)
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.6** (Orientation): subsection (a)1-8 is the minimum content of the New Employee Orientation Checklist.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.7** (Staff training)
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.8** (Staff coverage): no numeric ratio or awake-overnight rule was found in 10:44A.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.9** (Records of individuals receiving services): the remaining required contents and any retention period were not read.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.10** (Individual financial records: personal funds): confirm the current subsection.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-3.1** (Advocacy and rights: General requirements): includes compliance with the Developmentally Disabled Rights Act, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-1 et seq., and the use of a Human Rights Committee under N.J.A.C. 10:41A.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-4.3** (Individual Habilitation Plan (IHP))
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-5.1 to 5.8** (Subchapter 5, Health and Safety): the individual section text was not fully read, so confirm each section number and requirement before citing it individually.
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-5.2** (Prescription medication)
- **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-6.1 to 6.17** (Subchapter 6, Fire Safety and Physical Environment): confirm each section, including drill frequency, before citing it individually.

**Related cites named in the rules**
- N.J.A.C. 10:44B (scope exclusion: community care residences)
- Danielle's Law, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-5.1 et seq.; N.J.A.C. 10:42A (medical emergencies)
- N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6 (controlled dangerous substance testing; exchange of contact information with family/guardians)
- N.J.A.C. 10:41-2 (confidentiality)

**Rule status and enforcement**
- **58 N.J.R. 1193(b)**: N.J.A.C. 10:44A was readopted effective February 17, 2026 (new expiration February 17, 2033). DHS stated further rulemaking may be necessary.
- **P.L.2025, c.280**: expands DHS enforcement authority over developmental disability providers (January 2026). The statute text was not reviewed, so counsel should read its penalty provisions.

**Medicaid / DDD and federal requirements**
- **NJ FamilyCare Comprehensive Demonstration (Section 1115); HCBS Statewide Transition Plan Addendum #3**: authority for the DDD Supports Program / Community Care Program. The HCBS settings transition plan applies to 10:44A homes.
- **DDD - Apply to Become a Provider**: Combined Application and Individual Supports approval, with at least 24 months of documented direct-care service history.
- **DDD FFS FAQ: Becoming a Medicaid Provider**: an agency must be Medicaid-approved before submitting claims.
- **21st Century Cures Act §12006(a) (42 U.S.C. 1396b(l))**: Electronic Visit Verification, applied in NJ to DDD Individual Supports, In-Home Respite and Community Based Supports through HHAeXchange, with a Live-In Worker Attestation available where the worker lives with the person served.
- **DDD Division Update, August 20, 2026**: annual financial statement audit (GAAS) for agencies claiming $350,000 or more in combined CCP and Supports Program reimbursement. The Fiscal Sustainability Report is due 120 days after the state fiscal year ends.
- **DDD Division Update, January 22, 2026; iRecord Rate Change (1/1/2026)**: DSP and DSP Supervisor wage pass-through of about $0.46/hr as a base-wage increase, no later than 3/1/2026, with retroactive pay. It cannot be paid as a bonus or used for operating expenses.
- **NJ DHS Office of Licensing (OPIA) provider page**: annual and unannounced inspections, increasing beginning 2026. Partial compliance can produce a provisional license, and two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal. Housing must be cleared with DDD's Office of Housing and Resource Development before acquisition.

### Regulators and contacts

| **NJ DHS Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services (DMAHS)** | NJ Medicaid agency; operates the EVV program; Medicaid provider registration and claims | https://www.nj.gov/humanservices/dmahs/providers-stakeholders/overview/evv.shtml |

**[AGENCY NAME]** should verify each phone number and email address with the regulator before listing it in the final manual, and should add any county or local contacts (for example, the local fire official and Community Services Office) that apply.

### Official policy checklist and review documents

No separate Office of Licensing policy checklist form was found. The regulation itself is the review standard, so the documents used to review this manual are:

1. **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2, Development and maintenance of procedure manual**, especially **subsection (b)1-22**, the enumerated list of required manual contents. Under 10:44A-1.4(i), the Office of Licensing approves the manual if it meets 10:44A-2.2. Text last amended 55 N.J.R. 171(a), eff. 2/6/2023; chapter readopted eff. 2/17/2026.
2. **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.6(a)1-8, Orientation**: the minimum content of the New Employee Orientation Checklist required by 2.2(b)4.
3. **N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(c)1.i and (i), Application for licensure**: the program description and table of organization, and the submission sequence. The procedure manual goes to the Office of Licensing before opening, and job descriptions go to DDD after manual approval.

**Appendix A** maps every official item above to the specific policy in this manual that satisfies it. Items from 10:44A-2.2(b)1-22 are listed in order, and 2.6(a)1-8 appears as sub-items under the orientation checklist. Use Appendix A to confirm complete coverage before submission and at each annual review.

### Keeping the manual compliant

- **Customize**: replace all **[AGENCY NAME]** and other placeholders with agency-specific information.
- **Adopt**: the governing authority must formally adopt the manual and any later revisions.
- **Keep current**: review procedures at least annually (10:44A-2.2(a)), and recheck against the current N.J.A.C. text, DDD updates and Office of Licensing guidance. The chapter was readopted in 2026 and further rulemaking is possible.
- **Train**: all staff must be trained on the policies relevant to their duties (10:44A-2.7(c)), with training records kept as 10:44A-2.7(e) requires.
- **Legal review**: have counsel review the manual, particularly in light of P.L.2025, c.280 and the rule sections flagged above as not fully confirmed.

citations.title: Purpose and scope
citations.requirement: Chapter sets minimum requirements for residential services to people with DD. It applies to provider-managed group homes and supervised apartments. Community care residences (Family Care/Skill Development in a private home) are licensed under 10:44B. Head-injury residences fall under 10:44C. Licensing is voluntary where no resident needs personal guidance, as decided by the planning team.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines the terms the manual must use. Community residence: up to 16 individuals, not on the grounds of or immediately adjacent to public institutions serving a similar population. Supervised apartment: up to 4 individuals per apartment. Full license: up to one year. Also defines Abuse, Exploitation, Central Registry, Critical information, Direct support professional, Governing authority, Community agency head, Executive director, Behavior support plan, Falsification, Fiduciary capacity, Guardian, Authorization to operate (permits operation past license expiration when an inspection is delayed), Eviction, and Service plan/planning team.

citations.title: Application for licensure
citations.requirement: (a) Combined Application to Become a Medicaid/DDD Approved Provider plus the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider. (b) No agency head may be paid or contracted until criminal history clearance under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-63 through 69; owner/licensee also checked if different from the agency head. (c)(1) Application contents include a table of organization, CVs, owners, 24 months of service history with survey results and plans of correction, penalties/fines record, CPA examination for two fiscal years, and 3 professional references each. (d)(1) 45 days to complete or the application may be denied, with a 6-month bar on reapplying. (g) Written decision within 60 calendar days. (i) The procedure manual goes to the Office of Licensing before opening, then job descriptions go to DDD. (j) No operation without Office of Licensing authorization. (k) DHS inspection without limitation or notice. (l) Annual on-site inspection. (m) No license after denial by any State agency for substantial noncompliance. (n) No license if a final finding of discrimination exists.

citations.title: General requirements
citations.requirement: (a) The licensee's purposes and a description of its services must be made available to individuals, parents, guardians, advocates and the general public. Other subsections of 2.1 were not read.

citations.title: Development and maintenance of procedure manual
citations.requirement: (a) Licensee develops and implements a written procedure manual. Procedures are reviewed annually. Each procedure is designed on normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning. Each has a unique title, purpose, sequential steps, staff responsibilities and reporting/recording requirements. (b) Required contents: 1 philosophy; 2 table of organization; 3 Central Registry compliance; 4 New Employee Orientation Checklist; 5 major emergency/evacuation plan, including indoor air below 68F or above 82F for four consecutive hours; 6 medical emergencies with a 9-1-1 call for life-threatening emergencies (Danielle's Law, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-5.1 et seq.; N.J.A.C. 10:42A); 7 emergency coverage/on-call; 8 unusual incident reporting with a written prohibition on abuse, neglect and exploitation and the obligation to report each allegation; 9 investigations; 10 fiscal management of personal funds; 11 safekeeping of valuables; 12 list and schedule of charges and fees; 13 complaint/grievance procedure with at least two levels, the last involving the licensee or executive director; 14 separate internal communication/critical-information log; 15 admissions per 10:44A-4; 16 confidentiality per N.J.A.C. 10:41-2; 17 medication administration and self-medication; 18 controlled dangerous substance testing of employees (N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5); 19 exchange of contact information with involved family/guardians (N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6); 20 Child Abuse Registry check; 21 video/audio monitoring of common areas, if applicable; 22 continuous quality improvement system.

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: Personnel requirements, including employee screening. All employees who may contact individuals must comply with the screening requirements. A provider-hosted copy of the 2023 text shows a TB screen (Mantoux 5 TU PPD or IGRA blood test) within one year before or upon starting work, with written results submitted to the licensee. The 2005 text also required annual repeat testing, so confirm the current subsection letter and any repeat interval.

citations.title: Minimum staff qualifications
citations.requirement: (a) Licensee or executive director has a bachelor's degree, five years of progressive DD management experience (at least two supervisory at a senior/administrative level), and knowledge of program design, staff development and fiscal/qualitative standards. (b) Residence supervisor has a high school diploma or equivalent plus one year of DD experience. (c) DSPs are 18 or older with a high school diploma or equivalent. (d) DSPs can communicate with the individuals they work with. (e) DSPs can provide the direct assistance or training required. (f) Licensee verifies professional credentials required by law for employed or contracted professionals.

citations.title: Staff training
citations.requirement: (a) Within 90 days of employment each DSP completes Division basic training: DDD Shifting Expectations, preventing abuse and neglect, first aid and CPR from an ECC-compliant entity, each with a valid certificate on file. (b) Medication training and demonstrated competency come before administering any medication, and competency is shown annually. (c) Training in all relevant policies not covered in orientation. (d) Specialized training within 90 days of employment: feeding techniques (feeding tube duties delegated to nursing), mobility devices and transport, seizure/physical/medical needs, mental health needs, and behavior support plans. (e) Training records kept in the administrative office with a curriculum/training plan, dated trainer and trainee signatures, and Division-required results. (f) Additional training is allowed without Division approval. (g) Training under (c) is delivered by a qualified trainer.

citations.title: Staff coverage
citations.requirement: (a) A written staff schedule for at least two weeks is available at each residence with full staff names. It shows on-site coverage per the program description, and an in-charge employee for each shift. Temporary agency staff may not be designated in-charge unless all 2.7 training is complete and a written policy states the licensee assumes responsibility and liability. (b) Each required specialized training is completed by at least one person on each shift. (c) Staff need not be on site when no individuals are present, but trained, paid agency staff familiar with the individuals must be available for emergencies. (d) Group home/supervised apartment staff are on site whenever any individual is present, per supervision needs. (e) The staff residence/office of a supervised apartment program is located so response time fits supervision needs. No numeric ratio or awake-overnight rule was found in 10:44A.

citations.title: Records of individuals receiving services
citations.requirement: (a) An individual file is kept for each individual receiving services. (b) Files for group home and supervised apartment residents are kept at the residence. Contents include full name, DOB and sex; Social Security and Medicaid/insurance numbers; and dates of admission, readmission, transfer or discharge. The remaining required contents and any retention period were not read.

citations.title: Individual financial records: personal funds
citations.requirement: The licensee keeps a written record of all financial arrangements and transactions involving individuals' entrusted funds. Each individual and guardian has access to it on request, and copies are provided on request. The 2005 text also required the licensee to manage funds so as not to jeopardize benefit entitlements. Confirm the current subsection.

citations.title: Advocacy and rights: General requirements
citations.requirement: (a) Services recognize that people with disabilities have the same rights as other citizens, and exercising rights is never a cause for retribution. (b) Licensee complies with the Developmentally Disabled Rights Act, N.J.S.A. 30:6D-1 et seq. (c) Staff are familiar with and observe the rights listed in the Division's rights document. The licensee provides the rights document and gets acknowledgments on admission. (d) Individuals receive training and support to understand options, make choices and exercise rights. Rights are not limited because an individual has a guardian or family. (e) The licensee uses a Human Rights Committee under N.J.A.C. 10:41A. House rules involve the affected individuals, are necessary for order, and do not infringe on others' rights.

citations.title: Individual Habilitation Plan (IHP)
citations.requirement: (a) The licensee has and implements a procedure for developing, implementing, reviewing and evaluating each individual's habilitation or service plan under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-10 et seq. (b) The plan and monthly documentation of progress are kept in the individual's record. (c) The comprehensive IHP includes 14 elements: cover page; evaluation summaries; progress on prior goals; preferences, capabilities and needs; goals; measurable sequential objectives; method for each objective; team members and responsible persons; services with start dates, duration and frequency; barriers; guardianship review; meeting summary/addendum (disagreement may be noted); attendance sign-off; and authorization for approved individual expenses.

citations.title: Subchapter 5 - Health and Safety
citations.requirement: The subchapter spans 10:44A-5.1 to 5.8 per the LII table of contents. A DHS 2/14/2023 webinar says 5.1(g)8-9 added a CPR mask and protective gloves to first aid kit requirements. The 2005 text had 5.1 General health care and 5.3 Over-the-counter medications. The rest of the subchapter text was not read, so confirm each section number and requirement (health care, OTC medications, food/diets, restraint/behavioral supports, incident rules) before citing it individually.

citations.title: Prescription medication
citations.requirement: (a) Individuals self-administer to the extent possible, as determined by the planning team, documented in the record and following licensee procedure. (b) If the individual cannot, the licensee or designee assists and supervises administration as prescribed. (c) A record is kept of all medication administered, including individual's name, date and medication name. For PRN medication the label must show name, date, medication, dosage, interval, maximum amount per 24 hours, stop date where appropriate, and conditions for giving it. An Advanced Practice Nurse may prescribe (2023 amendment).

citations.title: Subchapter 6 - Fire Safety and Physical Environment
citations.requirement: The subchapter spans 6.1 to 6.17 per the LII table of contents. Rule text seen indicates the licensee must obtain documentation of any required Fire Official inspection and registration with the Department of Community Affairs, and a certificate from the local enforcing authority (or documentation that none is issued). The individual section text, including drill frequency, was not read, so confirm each section number and requirement before citing it individually.

citations.title: Manual of Standards for Community Care Residences (scope exclusion)
citations.requirement: Owner-occupied Family Care/Skill Development living arrangements are licensed under 10:44B and not 10:44A. This manual covers provider-managed homes and apartments only.

citations.title: Notice of Readoption, N.J.A.C. 10:44A
citations.requirement: 10:44A was readopted effective February 17, 2026 (new expiration February 17, 2033). DHS stated further rulemaking may be necessary. The section text cited here is the 2023-amended text, so recheck against the current rule each year.

citations.title: Enhanced Human Services enforcement authority over developmental disability providers (Jan 2026)
citations.requirement: Expands DHS enforcement authority over DD providers. The statute text was not reviewed, so counsel should read the penalty provisions.

citations.title: Electronic Visit Verification
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care/home health services. NJ applies it to DDD Individual Supports, In-Home Respite and Community Based Supports through HHAeXchange. A Live-In Worker Attestation allows exclusion where the worker lives with the person served.

citations.title: Authority for DDD Supports Program / Community Care Program

citations.cite: DDD - Apply to Become a Provider
citations.title: Combined Application / Individual Supports provider approval
citations.requirement: Agencies that want to run a licensed residential setting submit the Combined Application and select Individual Supports. At least 24 months of documented direct-care service history is required, including survey/audit results and plans of correction.

citations.title: Annual audit and Fiscal Sustainability Report
citations.requirement: An annual financial statement audit is required for agencies claiming $350,000 or more in combined CCP and Supports Program reimbursement. The audit follows GAAS. The Fiscal Sustainability Report is due 120 days after the state fiscal year ends (about October 30).

citations.cite: DDD Division Update, January 22, 2026; iRecord Rate Change (1/1/2026)
citations.title: DSP/DSP Supervisor wage pass-through
citations.requirement: Rates for nine agency-provided services rose 1/1/2026. Agencies must pass through about $0.46/hr as a base-wage increase to DSPs and DSP Supervisors no later than 3/1/2026, with retroactive pay. It cannot be paid as a bonus or used for operating expenses.

citations.cite: NJ DHS Office of Licensing (OPIA) provider page
citations.title: Inspections, provisional licenses and enforcement posture
citations.requirement: Annual and unannounced inspections, which increase beginning 2026. Inspectors review staff files, schedules, credentials, background checks, physical plant and insurance documents. Partial compliance can produce a provisional license, and two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal. Housing must be cleared with DDD's Office of Housing and Resource Development before acquisition.

citations.title: Medicaid approval before billing
citations.requirement: An agency must be Medicaid-approved to submit claims for DDD services, and the same Combined Application is used for Medicaid and DDD approval. NJ Medicaid denies claims from providers without a Medicaid ID.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Program Director Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] community residences and supervised apartments licensed under N.J.A.C. 10:44A; governing authority, executive director, program/residence supervisors and all staff
policies.purpose: To state the philosophy, values and goals that direct [AGENCY NAME], to show lines of authority, responsibility and communication, and to define who holds final authority and who is in charge at all times, so that individuals receive safe, person-centered supports and licensing requirements are met.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] operates community residences and supervised apartments under N.J.A.C. 10:44A. This policy meets N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b)1 (a statement of philosophy, values and goals that governs the organization's direction and character) and N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b)2 (a table of organization that illustrates lines of authority, responsibility and communication).

Philosophy, values and goals (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b)1): [AGENCY NAME] believes that every person with a developmental disability is entitled to dignity, respect, safety, choice and the same opportunities for community life as any other New Jersey resident. Our values are person-centered planning, normalization, age-appropriate living, the least restrictive approach, informed choice, and zero tolerance for abuse, neglect and exploitation. Our goals are to (1) support each individual to live the life he or she chooses in a home that is truly his or her own; (2) support community participation, relationships and employment choice; (3) protect health and safety; (4) respect rights, privacy and decision-making; (5) employ qualified, trained and supervised staff; and (6) use data to keep improving. Every procedure in this manual is read in light of this statement.

Table of organization (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b)2): [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written table of organization, kept in GOV-03, that shows each position, to whom it reports, and the lines of communication among the governing authority, the executive director, program/residence supervisors, nursing and clinical contacts, and direct support professionals. The governing authority holds ultimate legal responsibility for the agency. The executive director (or licensee, where the licensee serves in that role) is responsible for day-to-day management and meets N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.5(a): a bachelor's degree, five years of progressive management experience in developmental disabilities (at least two of them supervisory at a senior or administrative level), and knowledge of program design, staff development and fiscal and qualitative standards. Terms are used as defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3.

Final authority and in-charge: The executive director holds final operational authority. When the executive director is absent, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or a written designee holds final authority. A named in-charge employee is designated for every shift at every residence (see STF-01 and STF-09). The agency keeps a written record of who holds each authority at all times.

definitions.definition: The owner, board of directors or other body with ultimate legal responsibility for [AGENCY NAME], as defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3.
The individual responsible for the overall operation and management of the agency or program, as defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3. [AGENCY NAME] uses the title [EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR TITLE].
A chart showing each position, reporting relationships, and the lines of authority, responsibility and communication.
The staff member designated in writing as responsible for the residence and the individuals on a given shift.
An employee who provides direct assistance, training and support to individuals, as defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3.

procedures: The governing authority adopts the statement of philosophy, values and goals in writing, records the adoption in its minutes, and places the statement at the front of this manual.

The governing authority appoints the executive director in writing. Before appointment, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] verifies the candidate's bachelor's degree, five-year progressive DD management history (including two supervisory years at a senior level) and fiscal and program knowledge, and files the evidence in the personnel record (see STF-10).

The executive director prepares the table of organization and keeps it current in GOV-03. It shows every position, reporting line and communication channel, including the governing authority, executive director, program/residence supervisors, nurse and clinical consultants, and DSPs.
The executive director defines in writing the duties of each position in a job description (see GOV-03) and checks that each duty has a position responsible for it.

The executive director designates in writing a person to hold final authority whenever the executive director is unavailable, with a backup. The designation lists the person's name, phone number and the dates covered. It is posted in the administrative office and given to all residence supervisors.

The program/residence supervisor at each site is the day-to-day manager of the residence. The supervisor holds at least a high school diploma or equivalent and one year of DD experience (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.5(b)). The supervisor enforces the schedule, supervises DSPs, implements each individual's service plan, and reports to the executive director.

For every shift, the residence supervisor names the in-charge employee on the posted staff schedule (see STF-01). That person knows who to call for authority when the executive director and supervisor are not on site.

The executive director holds a documented management meeting with residence supervisors at least monthly, or more often when needed, to review incidents, staffing, individual needs, quality data and compliance. Minutes are kept.

The executive director reports to the governing authority at least quarterly on census, incidents, inspection results, finances, quality data (GOV-05) and staffing, and records the report in the governing authority's minutes.

Lines of communication are followed as shown on the table of organization: DSP to in-charge employee, to residence supervisor, to executive director, to governing authority. Any employee may go directly to the executive director or governing authority with an abuse, neglect, exploitation or safety concern without retaliation (see BEH-03).
Critical information is passed through the internal communication log required by REC-03, not by word of mouth alone.

When any position or the owner/licensee changes, the executive director updates the table of organization within 10 business days, notifies the Office of Licensing and DDD as required (GOV-02, GOV-03), and ensures required criminal history clearance for any new agency head or owner.
The governing authority and executive director review the philosophy and the table of organization at least annually as part of the manual review in GOV-04, and sign and date the review.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts the philosophy, appoints and evaluates the executive director, provides adequate resources, receives quarterly reports and approves major policy.
Manages the agency, maintains the table of organization and job descriptions, designates the person holding final authority in the executive director's absence, and ensures licensing compliance.
Manages the residence, schedules and supervises staff, names the in-charge employee each shift, and reports to the executive director.
Is responsible for the residence and individuals on the shift, and follows the chain of communication.
Know the chain of authority and report concerns through it or directly to the executive director.

Statement of philosophy, values and goals (front of manual)
Current table of organization (GOV-03)
Written designation of final authority when the executive director is absent
Executive director credential verification file
Monthly management meeting minutes and quarterly governing authority reports
Posted staff schedules showing in-charge employees

policies.title: Licensure, Certification and Provider Agreements
policies.applies_to: [AGENCY NAME] governing authority, executive director and administrative staff responsible for licensing, Medicaid/DDD approval and housing
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] holds and maintains every license, approval and agreement needed before it serves or bills for any individual, and operates only within the scope of those approvals.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] will not own or operate a community residence unless the NJ DHS Office of Licensing has authorized it (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(j)), and will not bill for DDD services unless it is a Medicaid/DDD approved provider with an active Medicaid ID.

Scope. This manual applies to provider-managed community residences (up to 16 individuals per residence) and supervised apartments (up to 4 individuals per apartment) licensed under N.J.A.C. 10:44A, as defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3. A community residence is not located on the grounds of, or immediately adjacent to, a public institution serving a similar population. Owner-occupied Family Care or Skill Development living arrangements are licensed under N.J.A.C. 10:44B and are outside this manual (N.J.A.C. 10:44B; N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.1). Residences for people with traumatic brain injury fall under a separate chapter (10:44C) and are not operated under this manual. Licensing is voluntary only where the planning team determines that no resident needs personal guidance (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.1). [AGENCY NAME] will not claim voluntary status without the planning team's written determination.

Provider approval. [AGENCY NAME] applies through the Combined Application to Become a Medicaid/DDD Approved Provider, with the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider, and selects Individual Supports. The same application serves Medicaid and DDD approval, and at least 24 months of documented direct-care service history is required, with survey results and plans of correction. NJ Medicaid denies claims from providers without a Medicaid ID. Services are authorized under the NJ FamilyCare Comprehensive Demonstration (Section 1115), and the HCBS settings requirements apply to our homes.

License term. A full license is issued for up to one year. The Office of Licensing conducts annual on-site inspections, and the Department may inspect without limitation or notice (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(k), (l)). Authorization to operate, as defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3, allows operation past license expiration only when an inspection is delayed. [AGENCY NAME] does not assume it has such authorization without written confirmation. Partial compliance may result in a provisional license, and two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal. The chapter was readopted effective February 17, 2026 (58 N.J.R. 1193(b)), and DHS has said further rulemaking may be necessary, so this policy and all procedures are rechecked against the current rule at least annually.

definitions.definition: A provider-managed residence for up to 16 individuals with developmental disabilities, not on the grounds of or immediately adjacent to a public institution serving a similar population (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3).
An apartment arrangement serving up to 4 individuals per apartment with agency staff support (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3).
Written authorization permitting continued operation past license expiration when the Department's inspection is delayed (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3).
The DDD application to become a Medicaid/DDD approved provider, used with the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider.
The identifier issued by NJ Medicaid that is required to submit claims.

procedures: Before acquiring or leasing any property, the executive director confirms the site with DDD's Office of Housing and Resource Development, as required by the Department, and records the clearance in the licensing file.

The executive director confirms the planned program is within scope: a provider-managed home of 16 or fewer, or an apartment of 4 or fewer per apartment, not located on or adjacent to a public institution for a similar population.

The executive director compiles the application: table of organization, CVs, owner information, 24 months of service history with survey results and plans of correction, penalty and fine record, CPA examination for two fiscal years, and three professional references each. Completion target: [DATE].

The agency obtains criminal history clearance under N.J.S.A. 30:6D-63 through 69 for the agency head, and for the owner/licensee if different, before any payment or contract is made to that person (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(b)). The result is filed in the licensing file.

The executive director submits the Combined Application and the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider through DDD, selecting Individual Supports, and calendars the 45-day deadline for missing elements. Missing material is submitted within 45 days to avoid denial and the six-month reapplication bar (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(d)(1)). The agency expects a written decision within 60 calendar days of a complete application (1.4(g)).

The agency confirms it has no denial by any State agency for substantial noncompliance and no final finding of discrimination that would bar a license (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(m), (n)), and reports any such history honestly in the application.
The agency submits the procedure manual to the Office of Licensing for approval before opening, then submits job descriptions to DDD (see GOV-03).

No individual is admitted and no service begins until the Office of Licensing authorizes operation in writing. The executive director places the license in the licensing file and posts or keeps it available as the Department directs.

The administrative staff member designated by [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms the Medicaid ID is active before any claim is submitted. A new admission that expects DDD billing does not proceed until the ID and authorization are confirmed (see PCS-01 and GOV-06).

The executive director calendars the license expiration date and requests renewal at least [NUMBER] days in advance. If an inspection is delayed, the executive director asks the Office of Licensing for written authorization to operate and files it.
The executive director confirms insurance, physical plant and personnel documents are current and available for inspection (see GOV-08).

After any provisional license, the executive director convenes the governing authority within 5 business days, adopts a corrective timeline, and monitors it weekly. The agency treats a second consecutive provisional license as a risk of non-renewal.
Each year, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] rechecks N.J.A.C. 10:44A, any 10:44A notices and any DDD provider circulars for changes, records the review date, and updates this manual through GOV-04.
Any change in owner, executive director, address, capacity or program type is reported to the Office of Licensing and DDD before it takes effect, or as the Department directs.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the application, ensures the agency does not operate without authorization, and reviews renewal status.
Prepares and files applications, maintains the license and Medicaid ID, tracks expirations, and manages changes.
Confirm Medicaid ID status and DDD authorizations before billing.
Keeps the license and required postings available at the residence.

DDD Office of Housing and Resource Development clearance
Written authorization to operate, if applicable
Annual rule recheck log

policies.title: Program Description, Table of Organization and Job Descriptions
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, executive director, residence supervisors and administrative staff
policies.purpose: To keep a current program description, table of organization and set of approved job descriptions that tell the Department, DDD and staff what services are provided, who provides them, and how supervision is assured to every individual.
policies.policy:
This policy meets N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3 (Program description), N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(i)2, and N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b)2.

1.3 (Program description): The program description is the document submitted to obtain a license. It describes the services provided to individuals and the staff coverage that assures supervision to every individual served, in accordance with each person's service plan. It is reviewed as part of the licensing inspection and is amended as necessary. [AGENCY NAME] keeps a current program description for each residence and for each supervised apartment program, consistent with N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.8, under which staff are on site whenever any individual is present, per supervision needs, and a supervised apartment program's staff residence or office is located so response time fits supervision needs.

1.4(i)2: After the Office of Licensing approves this manual, [AGENCY NAME] submits job descriptions to the Division of Developmental Disabilities for every position on the table of organization, for review and approval. The manual itself is submitted to the Office of Licensing before opening (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4(i)).

2.2(b)2: The table of organization illustrates lines of authority, responsibility and communication and matches the program description and job descriptions. It is updated whenever a position changes and resubmitted as DDD directs.

definitions.definition: The document submitted to obtain a license that describes services and the staff coverage assuring supervision to every individual, per the service plan, amended as necessary (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3).
A written statement of a position's title, qualifications, reporting line, duties and training requirements.
The individual's plan and the team that develops it, as defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3 (see PCS-02).

procedures: The executive director writes the program description for each residence and apartment program. It describes the services provided, the population served, the on-site staffing pattern and how supervision matches each individual's service plan.

The program description states staff coverage in terms the schedule can be checked against, such as on-site hours and in-charge designation, with no numeric ratio asserted unless DDD, the service plan or the agency's own commitment requires it. It addresses when individuals are away from the residence and how trained paid staff familiar with the individuals are available for emergencies.

For supervised apartments, the description states where the staff residence or office is located and the expected response time, and explains why that response time fits the supervision needs of the people served.
The executive director submits the program description with the licensing application (GOV-02) and keeps a copy in the licensing file and at each residence.
The executive director builds the table of organization showing every position and reporting line, using the format in GOV-01, and files it with the manual.

For each position, the executive director writes a job description that includes title, reporting line, minimum qualifications under N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.5 (see STF-10), duties, required trainings (see STF-04) and in-charge responsibilities where applicable.

After the Office of Licensing approves the manual, the executive director submits job descriptions for every position on the table of organization to DDD for review and approval, and records the date submitted.
The executive director files DDD's approval or comments, revises job descriptions as DDD directs, and resubmits within [NUMBER] days.
Each new hire receives the approved job description at hire and signs an acknowledgment, which is filed in the personnel record (STF-06).
The executive director amends the program description whenever services, capacity, staffing pattern or supervision approach changes, and notifies the Office of Licensing as directed.

When a position is added, eliminated or substantially changed, the executive director updates the table of organization and job description before the change takes effect and submits the revision to DDD.
The residence supervisor compares the posted two-week staff schedule to the program description each schedule period (STF-01) and reports any gap to the executive director immediately.
The executive director reviews the program description, table of organization and job descriptions annually during the manual review in GOV-04 and before each licensing renewal.

responsibilities.duty: Writes and amends the program description, table of organization and job descriptions, and submits them to the Office of Licensing and DDD.
Approves the program description and organizational changes.
Checks daily operation and the staff schedule against the program description, and reports gaps.
Maintain version control, file approvals and distribute job descriptions.

documentation: Current program description for each residence/program
Table of organization with revision dates
Job descriptions for all positions, with DDD submission and approval records
Signed job description acknowledgments
Annual review sign-off
Correspondence with the Office of Licensing and DDD

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control (Procedure Manual Standards)
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, executive director, residence supervisors and all authors and users of this procedure manual
policies.purpose: To make sure the procedure manual is written, implemented, reviewed and controlled as the rule requires, so every procedure is complete, easy to find, and consistent with current law.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] develops and implements this manual of written procedures to ensure the service delivery system complies with State law and the rules governing community residences for individuals with developmental disabilities. This policy meets the following checklist items:

- N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a): the licensee develops and implements a manual of written procedures that ensures compliance with State law and rules.
- N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a)1: procedures are reviewed annually and revised as necessary.
- N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a)2: each procedure is designed in accordance with the principles of normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction and person-centered planning, and is consistent with the organizational structure and management philosophy of the licensee.
- N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a)3.i: each procedure has a descriptive title that is unique, so each document can be easily referenced and retrieved.
- N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a)3.ii: each procedure explains its purpose.
- N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a)3.iii: each procedure describes the sequential steps required to complete a task or action.
- N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a)3.iv: each procedure assigns staff responsibilities at each step of implementation.
- N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a)3.v: each procedure states reporting and recording requirements for each person involved.

The manual is not a shelf document. Staff are trained on it and follow it, and the Office of Licensing may review it and staff practice at any inspection. Because 10:44A was readopted effective February 17, 2026 (58 N.J.R. 1193(b)), with DHS indicating further rulemaking may be necessary, and because the section text relied on here is the 2023-amended text, the agency rechecks every procedure against the current rule at least annually and whenever DHS publishes a notice or proposal.

definitions.definition: The agency's complete set of written procedures required by N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2.
A policy with a unique ID and title, version number, effective date and approver, kept under revision control.
Supporting people to live in ways as typical of their community and age peers as possible, with the least restrictive supports necessary.

procedures: The executive director owns the manual and assigns each policy a unique ID and unique descriptive title (for example, "GOV-04 Policy Review and Document Control"), listed in a master index (N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(a)3.i).

Every policy uses a standard template: purpose (2.2(a)3.ii); policy statement; definitions; numbered sequential steps (2.2(a)3.iii); responsibilities by role assigned at each step (2.2(a)3.iv); and documentation, reporting and recording requirements for each person involved (2.2(a)3.v).

The author drafts each policy and then answers a design check in writing before approval: Does it reflect normalization? Is it age appropriate? Is it the least restrictive approach? Does it start from person-centered planning? Is it consistent with our organizational structure and philosophy (GOV-01)? (2.2(a)2).
The executive director confirms the policy against the cited rule text and DDD requirements, and records the citations checked.
The governing authority approves the manual and any significant change in its minutes. The approval date, version and approver are recorded on each policy.
Before opening, the executive director submits the manual to the Office of Licensing as required (see GOV-02) and records the approval.
The executive director trains all staff on policies relevant to their jobs at orientation (STF-03) and whenever a policy changes. Staff sign a training acknowledgment.

A current copy of the full manual is kept at the administrative office. A copy of policies needed in an emergency or every shift (emergency, medication, incident, abuse reporting, rights) is kept at each residence in the location named by the residence supervisor.

Each policy is reviewed in full at least annually (2.2(a)1). The executive director sets a review calendar so that GOV, IR, PCS, HW, BEH, ENV, STF and REC policies are each reviewed by [MONTH] each year, and signs the review date on each policy.

Reviewers consider: changes in law or DDD guidance; inspection findings and plans of correction (GOV-08); incident, grievance and quality data (GOV-05); staff and individual feedback; and any practice that departs from the written procedure.
Any needed revision is drafted, approved and dated. The old version is archived (not deleted) and marked superseded with the date.

An urgent change (for example, after an incident or a new DHS directive) is issued by the executive director immediately by written notice, and staff acknowledge it within [NUMBER] business days. The change is added to the manual at the next revision cycle at the latest.
At least once a year, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] rechecks N.J.A.C. 10:44A and any 10:44A rulemaking notices, including 58 N.J.R. 1193(b) follow-up, and records the date and result in the revision log.

Residence supervisors observe practice against policy during monthly visits and report discrepancies. Where practice and policy differ, either practice is corrected or the policy is revised through this process.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the manual and substantive changes.
Owns the manual, assigns IDs, runs the annual review, maintains the revision log, and rechecks rule text.
Uses the template, completes the design check, cites the rule, and signs the review.
Keeps the on-site manual current, trains staff on changes, and monitors practice against policy.
Read, follow and acknowledge policies.

documentation: Master index of policies with IDs, titles, versions and effective dates
Revision log and archive of superseded versions
Annual review sign-offs
Design check records (normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction, person-centered planning)
Governing authority approvals
Staff policy training acknowledgments
Annual rule recheck record

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, executive director, residence supervisors, nursing and clinical staff and all staff who collect or use quality data
policies.purpose: To operate a continuous quality improvement system that finds opportunities to improve services and supports and resolves identified problems, using data and the voices of individuals, families and staff.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] operates a continuous quality improvement (CQI) system to identify opportunities to improve services and supports and to resolve identified problems. This policy meets N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b)22 and each of its required elements:

- 2.2(b)22.i: a written plan that identifies how data is collected, analyzed and used to determine patterns that identify process or systemic problems requiring further in-depth review (the CQI Plan, Procedures 1-5).
- 2.2(b)22.ii: input from a variety of sources, including persons receiving services, family members and others (Procedures 6-7).
- 2.2(b)22.iii: a written summary of satisfaction surveys (Procedure 8).
- 2.2(b)22.iv: a written summary of outcomes assessments (Procedure 9).
- 2.2(b)22.v: an action plan based upon the analysis of items i through iv (Procedures 10-12).

The CQI system also supports person-centered, community-based service and settings expectations applicable to HCBS (42 CFR 441.301(c)) and prepares the agency for annual and unannounced inspections by the Office of Licensing, which review staff files, schedules, credentials, background checks, physical plant and insurance documents. Death review is part of the CQI system and follows the procedure in HW-05.

definitions.definition: A planned, ongoing process of collecting and analyzing data, finding patterns, acting on them and checking results.
A structured review of whether individuals are achieving the goals and outcomes in their service plans and life satisfaction.
A pattern across individuals, residences, shifts or time that points to a process failure rather than an isolated event.
A review of every death to identify contributing factors, preventable causes and system improvements, following HW-05.

procedures: The executive director appoints a CQI Committee that includes the executive director, residence supervisors, the nurse or health care coordinator, at least one DSP, and, where they are willing, an individual receiving services and a family member or guardian. Meetings are held at least quarterly. [NAME] is the CQI coordinator.

The CQI coordinator keeps a written CQI Plan, approved by the governing authority, that lists each data source, who collects it, how often, and how it is analyzed. Data sources include reportable and unusual incidents (BEH-04), injuries, medication errors and omissions (HW-01), emergency room visits and hospital stays (HW-04), restraint and rights-restriction records (BEH-02, IR-02), grievances and complaints (IR-03), missing-person events (BEH-06), fire drills (ENV-02), staffing and vacancy data (STF-01), training completion (STF-04), billing and documentation reviews (GOV-06), inspection findings and plans of correction (GOV-08), and deaths (HW-05).
Residence supervisors submit their data to the CQI coordinator by the [DAY] of each month on the CQI Data Form.
The CQI coordinator tabulates the data by individual, residence, shift, time of day, staff and type, and compares it with prior periods to find trends.

The CQI Committee reviews the data at each meeting and decides which patterns are potential process or systemic problems that need a more in-depth review, such as a repeated medication error on a particular shift or a rise in falls at one site. The decision and reason are recorded in the minutes.

Input is gathered from a variety of sources: individuals, family members, guardians, staff, the planning team and community partners. Methods include satisfaction surveys, individual interviews with support for communication needs (IR-09), family contact, staff meetings, suggestion mechanisms and grievance data.

Individuals are given real opportunities to give feedback in a format that fits them, with support if they want it. Staff do not complete the survey for an individual who can answer, and no individual is penalized for what he or she says.

At least annually, the CQI coordinator distributes satisfaction surveys to individuals, families/guardians and staff, and writes a summary of the results, including response numbers and themes. The written summary is dated and filed.

At least annually, the CQI coordinator, with each individual's planning team, compiles an outcomes assessment. It looks at progress on service plan goals, community participation, employment choice, health outcomes, choice and rights, and satisfaction. The coordinator writes a summary across all individuals and residences without revealing private information beyond what is needed.

Using the data analysis, input, satisfaction summary and outcomes summary, the CQI Committee writes an action plan. Each action lists the problem, the cause found, the action, the person responsible, the due date and the measure of success.
The executive director assigns actions, gives the resources needed, and reports the action plan to the governing authority at least quarterly.

The CQI coordinator reviews the status of each action at every meeting, measures whether the problem improved, and keeps an action open until the measure shows improvement. Unresolved problems are escalated to the governing authority.

For every death, the executive director convenes a mortality review within [NUMBER] days of the death, following HW-05, which includes the circumstances, health history, recent care, incident and investigation findings, and any DHS or DDD review. Findings and prevention actions are added to the CQI action plan.
Any individual-level safety concern identified in CQI review is handled immediately under the relevant policy and is not held for the quarterly meeting.
The CQI Plan, data forms, summaries and action plan are reviewed and updated annually under GOV-04, and are available to the Office of Licensing and DDD on request.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the CQI Plan, reviews quarterly reports and ensures resources for action plans.
Leads the CQI system, convenes mortality review, and ensures actions are completed.
Collects data, writes summaries, tracks the action plan and keeps records.
Submit data on time and carry out site actions.
Provide health and medication data and participate in mortality review.
Are invited to give input and to serve on the committee.

documentation: Written CQI Plan
Monthly CQI Data Forms
CQI Committee minutes
Satisfaction survey results and written summary
Outcomes assessment and written summary
CQI action plan with status tracking
Mortality review reports
Quarterly governing authority CQI reports

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing, EVV and Service Documentation
policies.applies_to: Executive director, billing and administrative staff, residence supervisors and direct support professionals who deliver or document billed services
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] bills Medicaid/DDD only for authorized services actually delivered and documented, uses Electronic Visit Verification where required, and prevents false claims.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] is paid fee-for-service for DDD Individual Supports. Services are authorized under the NJ FamilyCare Comprehensive Demonstration (Section 1115), which replaced the former 1915(c) waiver, and the State's HCBS settings requirements apply to our homes.

Before billing. The agency must be a Medicaid-approved provider to submit claims. NJ Medicaid denies claims from providers without a Medicaid ID. [AGENCY NAME] does not admit anyone expecting billing until the Medicaid ID is active and the DDD authorization is in hand.

Billing. We bill only after services are delivered, only for services authorized for that individual, and only for what the documentation supports. Claims are reconciled to DDD authorizations monthly. Procedure codes, units and rates are confirmed with DDD (DDD.FeeForService@dhs.nj.gov); we do not rely on an assumed rate.

EVV. Electronic Visit Verification is required under the 21st Century Cures Act (42 U.S.C. 1396b(l)) and applies in New Jersey to DDD Individual Supports, In-Home Respite and Community Based Supports through HHAeXchange. Staff who deliver EVV-covered services record visits in EVV. A Live-In Worker Attestation is used only where the worker actually lives with the person served.

False claims. Knowingly submitting a false claim, or retaining an overpayment, violates the federal False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. 3729) and State law. Falsifying records is prohibited and is a ground for discipline up to termination and for reporting to authorities. Staff who report billing concerns in good faith are protected from retaliation.

definitions.definition: Payment for each authorized service delivered, rather than a capitated or lump-sum payment.
An electronic system that records the type of service, individual, date, location, worker and start/end time of a visit; DDD uses HHAeXchange.
A signed attestation permitting exclusion from EVV when the worker lives with the person served.
Making, altering or omitting a record entry to misstate what occurred, as defined in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3.

procedures: The executive director confirms the agency's Medicaid/DDD approval and Medicaid ID are active before the first admission (GOV-02) and records the confirmation date.

At intake, billing staff verify the individual's DDD eligibility and the written DDD authorization for the service, including type, dates and units, and enter them in the authorization tracker. No billing begins for a service not yet authorized.

The executive director confirms procedure codes, units and rates for each service with DDD (DDD.FeeForService@dhs.nj.gov) and records the answer and date. Billing staff use only confirmed codes and rates.
[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] assigns EVV users, sets up HHAeXchange accounts for every worker delivering EVV-covered service, and trains each worker before first use (see STF-03 and STF-04).

For each EVV-covered visit, the DSP records visit start and end in HHAeXchange at the time of service, from the correct location. A DSP does not record EVV for a visit he or she did not make or for time not worked.

A manual EVV correction is made only by the residence supervisor or designee, with a written reason (for example, a device failure) and a note of who authorized it. The executive director reviews all corrections monthly.

A Live-In Worker Attestation is used only when the worker lives with the person served. The executive director reviews the circumstances before using it, retains the signed attestation, and ends its use if the situation changes.

Each DSP documents the services delivered during the shift in the daily record as set out in PCS-03, in a contemporaneous, factual way, and signs. The documentation shows what was provided, when, and by whom, and matches the service plan.

The residence supervisor reviews daily documentation at least weekly for completeness, signature and consistency with the schedule and EVV, and corrects or escalates gaps within [NUMBER] business days.
Billing staff prepare claims only from verified, completed documentation. A second person reviews the claim batch against the authorization, schedule and EVV record before submission.
Claims are submitted within the period DDD allows. Billing staff track each claim to payment and investigate any denial or rejection within [NUMBER] business days.
Each month, billing staff reconcile claims and payments to the DDD authorization (units authorized, used and remaining) and report variances to the executive director, who decides on correction.

If an overpayment or billing error is found, the executive director stops further billing of the item, quantifies it, and reports and returns the overpayment to the payer as required. The matter and corrective steps are documented.

Any employee who suspects a false claim, missing documentation or falsification reports it to the executive director or the governing authority. Retaliation is prohibited and violators are disciplined.

The executive director conducts or arranges an internal documentation and billing review at least quarterly using a sample of records and reports results to the CQI Committee (GOV-05). The agency cooperates with DDD, NJ Medicaid and audit requests (see GOV-07).
The executive director rechecks DDD circulars and the EVV page for changes each quarter and updates this policy through GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures Medicaid compliance, confirms rates and codes with DDD, reviews EVV corrections and handles overpayments.
Verify authorizations, prepare claims from documentation, reconcile monthly and track denials.
Reviews daily documentation and EVV records weekly and authorizes manual corrections.
Record EVV accurately in real time and document services truthfully.
Oversees compliance and receives reports of billing issues.

DDD authorizations and authorization tracker
Rate/code confirmations from DDD
